mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES continues to recover from its recent trough, weekday discretionary shopping will rise with commuting volume and lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The signal should be strongest when TRANSIT also stops falling, because coordinated return-to-work behavior increases nearby retail trips.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -56.3 to -47.4 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the prior four-week mean despite a sustained 2-week increase in WORKPLACES and a stabilization in TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL remains elevated, consumers substitute toward home-based activity and reduce visits to retail and recreation venues, keeping RETAIL_REC below its recent average over the next two weeks. This mechanism fails if residential time drops back toward baseline while retail visits still do not recover.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is persistently positive across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days even though RESIDENTIAL stays above its recent four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: A further drop in TRANSIT below its already depressed level indicates renewed access frictions or mobility tightening, and that should pull RETAIL_REC down over the next four weeks. The effect is falsified if retail remains flat or improves while transit continues to weaken.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -60 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was -62.0 in t-1w and -55.0 in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is higher over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days even after TRANSIT stays below -60 for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upswing in PARKS activity signals favorable weather and outdoor substitution, which diverts discretionary time away from malls and dining and lowers RETAIL_REC within one to two weeks. The effect should be visible only when PARKS is above its recent average for at least two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS stays above 30 for 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS spiked to 46.0 in t-2w and remained positive thereafter
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not weaken within 7 to 14 days after PARKS remains above 30 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rebound in GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES indicates broader out-of-home circulation that should spill into more retail visits over the next four weeks. The mechanism is strongest when both series improve together rather than in isolation.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -14.1 to -8.6 while WORKPLACES improved from -56.3 to -47.4 in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its prior four-week mean even though GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES both rise for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If RETAIL_REC is more than 10 points above its recent average while TRANSIT remains deeply negative, the retail rebound is likely a temporary diversion from local driving rather than a broad demand recovery. In that case RETAIL_REC should reverse downward over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC rises above -55 while TRANSIT stays below -50
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -62.1 to -50.3 in t-0w while TRANSIT stayed at -55.0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues rising for 14 days after crossing above -55 even though TRANSIT remains below -50.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stops improving and turns back down after a short rebound, commuter-linked shopping demand will fade and RETAIL_REC will decline over the next month. The mechanism is regime-specific to partial reopening, where office mobility is the main lead indicator.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls by more than 5 points week-on-week after a rebound
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES remains far below baseline and fell sharply to -56.3 in t-1w before recovering to -47.4
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES dropping again after a brief rebound.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained combination of rising PARKS and falling RESIDENTIAL indicates households are spending more time outside the home, which should support higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The effect should fail when parks strength is offset by no change in residential time.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS remains positive while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated around 16 to 19
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 28 days even though PARKS stays above its recent mean and RESIDENTIAL trends down.
